Ben & team — quick notes after skimming the proposal and comparing to our FinSight data: 

Pros (CloudCents):
- Cleaner UI for cross-account cost attribution and better out-of-the-box tagging support
- Aggregation module addresses current duplicate-ingest problem we measured (could reduce storage/ingest compute)
- Faster implementation estimate (4 weeks) which is attractive for this quarter

Cons / unknowns:
- Pricing scale assumptions look optimistic; the $45k base assumes steady tokenization across months — risky if our burst months spike
- Limited support for on-prem telemetry ingestion (we do have constrained regions)
- FinSight matrix (attached) still shows better native AWS cost-anomaly detection and built-in FinOps policy automation

Recommendation: Run a 6-week pilot with the aggregator enabled on a constrained scope (two org accounts) to validate the 15% savings claim before committing to a 12-month term. If CloudCents can reduce the first-year cost by ~20% via discounts or credits for implementation, move to a standard 12-month SaaS contract.

I'll volunteer to run the pilot metrics and dashboarding. Need SC access and a test billing export.

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer

Thanks — a few procurement/legal points to surface: 

1) SOW clarity: CloudCents' draft SOW needs explicit IP/data handling language for billing exports; add an appendix for retention and deletion timelines.
2) Payment terms: try for Net 45 vs their default Net 30 given PS is front-loaded.
3) Discount target: aim for 18–22% off list in year 1 (including implementation credit). Anything under 15% becomes harder to justify vs FinSight.
4) Contract length: stick to 12 months with a 60-day opt-out clause tied to SLA breaches. We can consider 24 months only if they include deeper implementation credits.

I've attached a proposed SOW template with the clauses we usually use (proposed-SOW-cloudcents.docx). I'll open a procurement ticket and loop Legal.
